idea: A minimalist tool that turns lectures into interactive polls and quizzes.
assumptions: English-first, global audience of educators; 1–2 syllables preferred
No abbreviations unless they read as standalone words
Standalone product, not part of a parent brand
architecture_recommendation: Standalone name: it targets educators directly, needs its own app listing and domain, and has no parent brand to lean on.

top_10.name: Numo
top_10.rationale: Short, precise, modern; a subtle numeric cue without being literal. Four round letters make a strong wordmark.
linguistic_notes: No known negative meaning in English; check other target languages before shortlisting
risks: Light maths association may read as quantitative-only

top_10.name: Verveo
top_10.rationale: Built on 'verve'; confident and smooth, smart without sounding academic.
linguistic_notes: Three syllables; stress may drift to the second syllable for some speakers
risks: Close to 'Verve' brands in other categories

top_10.name: Quillix
top_10.rationale: Hints at writing and lectures with a modern edge; distinctive in the category.
linguistic_notes: Fails the radio test for some listeners: 'Quilix' or 'Kwillix' are likely misspellings
risks: The -ix ending edges toward a tech cliché

top_10.name: Vetra
top_10.rationale: Crisp and modern; feels like a precise tool brand.
risks: Abstract meaning needs a strong tagline

top_10.name: Pollis
top_10.rationale: Directly tied to polls without using the plain word; very clear.
linguistic_notes: Sounds like 'polis' (city-state); may be heard as a surname in some regions

top_10.name: Lumor
top_10.rationale: Calm and smart; a soft cue to light and insight.
linguistic_notes: Could be heard as 'rumour' or 'humour' by some listeners
risks: Many lum- names exist in software

top_10.name: Murmur
top_10.rationale: The sound of a room responding at once; suggests live participation without saying 'poll'. Repeated syllable makes a rhythmic wordmark.
linguistic_notes: The 'ur' vowel is harder for some non-native speakers
risks: Common English word, likely used by other brands
Can read as quiet or indistinct

top_10.name: Quietly
top_10.rationale: Matches the calm, minimal tone and stands out in a loud category.
linguistic_notes: Ordinary adverb; hard to own as a mark

top_10.name: Tallyn
top_10.rationale: From 'tally': precise and modern, a counting cue without the cliché.
linguistic_notes: Sounds like Tallinn, the Estonian capital
Spelling variants Talin and Tallin are likely
risks: Altered spelling must be explained aloud

top_10.name: Pivio
top_10.rationale: Short and clean; implies a pivot in the conversation.
linguistic_notes: Stress may be read as pi-VEE-oh

filtered_out.name: Swayze
filtered_out.reason: Kill screen: strongly associated with a well-known actor

filtered_out.name: Quizly
filtered_out.reason: Kill screen: category cliché (-ly) and descriptive

filtered_out.name: PollHub
filtered_out.reason: Kill screen: category cliché (-hub) and generic

next_steps: Pick 3 finalists and run trademark searches in the education and software classes for each target market.
Check company registries, app stores and social handles for the finalists.
Check .com plus one relevant open TLD for each finalist. Nothing here has been checked.
Say whether you prefer abstract or semi-descriptive names and the list can be refined.
